---
title: "Capture Files and Integrity"
format: gfm
---

Choose a format from the measurement you need to preserve, not only from the
file extension. Scope and MCA binary files share an `NDMA` header but have
different payloads and version rules.

## Format overview

| Capture | Format | Contents | Integrity evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope DMA | NDMA v1 `.bin` | Repeated complete timestamped int16 frames | Header geometry, exact frame alignment, no trailing partial frame |
| MCA legacy DMA | NDMA v1 `.bin` | Legacy gRPC/ZMQ 16-byte events | Alignment only; transport continuity is unverified |
| MCA IIO DMA | NDMA v2 `.bin` | Fixed 1,024 × opaque-16-byte frames | Authenticated JSON sidecar plus driver counters |
| MCA IIO DMA | `.h5` | Appendable canonical event dataset and embedded YAML | `committed_events`, `capture_complete`, run summary |
| MCA IIO DMA | `.root` | Canonical `events` TTree and embedded metadata | Run summary and successful close |
| MCA IIO DMA | Online-only | No file | GUI/session diagnostics only |
| Coincidence matrix | `.h5` or `.root` | Prompt/random/corrected matrices, axes, gates, calibration | Export metadata and session diagnostics |

## NDMA header and versions

The common 24-byte header stores magic, version, channel, recording timestamp,
and `frame_samples`. For Scope, `frame_samples` is a count of int16 words—not a
byte count. The first four int16 slots of every Scope record carry one little-
endian uint64 timestamp; the remaining words are waveform samples.

MCA NDMA uses `frame_samples=0`. Version 1 identifies the legacy semantic event
record. Version 2 identifies the current IIO opaque-record transport. The two
records are both 16 bytes but are not interchangeable.

## Scope recording constraints

Scope captures append complete frames to one file until stopped or storage
fails; they are not rotated at an application-defined size. The client rejects
partial frames rather than making an apparently valid truncated file.

NDMA v1 cannot describe decimation or alignment padding. IP122 periodic Scope
firmware advertises such a layout, so online Current DMA can consume it but the
legacy Scope NDMA writer rejects it explicitly. Do not alter the advertised
geometry or request a partial scan mask to force a file. A versioned Scope
format is required before that layout can be saved faithfully.

The headless `examples/dma_scope_periodic.py` recorder refuses to overwrite an
existing path or take over an active Scope, configures/auto-sets the channel,
and restores settings after capture. A maximum-frame ten-second recording can
be hundreds of megabytes.

## MCA structured output

The HDF5 writer appends canonical fields (`timestamp`, `long_gate`,
`short_gate`, `marker`, `zc_offset`, and signed `zc_estimation`) in bounded
batches. `committed_events` marks data visible to SWMR readers and
`capture_complete` becomes true only after successful finalization.

ROOT stores the same canonical fields in an `events` TTree. HDF5 and ROOT embed
the YAML configuration and the client record schema. They do not reinterpret
raw channels as calibrated energy.

Every file-producing MCA run writes a same-stem `.run.json` summary containing
channel, format, start/end time, record count, average rate, continuity state,
and transport diagnostics. A missing summary after a crash means the run was
not finalized; it is not evidence that the capture is complete.

## IIO list-mode sidecars

Binary IIO list mode additionally writes:

- a same-stem YAML hardware/application configuration;
- a JSON capture sidecar with frame geometry, client schema, capture SHA-256,
  completed-frame count, DMA fault, cumulative DMA error count, list deadtime,
  and continuity result;
- the format-independent `.run.json` summary.

The converter authenticates the JSON sidecar against the NDMA SHA-256 before
copying its diagnostics into HDF5. Do not separate or rename sidecars without
preserving their relationship to the capture.

## Continuity semantics

For current IIO list mode, a valid run requires all of the following:

- driver DMA fault is zero;
- streamed frame count equals driver completed-frame count;
- list deadtime is zero;
- only complete 16 KiB frames were accepted;
- the buffer stopped, drained, and closed successfully.

`dma_error_count` is cumulative since driver initialization; interpret it with
the current fault and run-local counters. IIO record counts include all slots
in the final complete frame, including indistinguishable zero padding. They are
not an exact accepted-pulse count.

Legacy gRPC runs are labelled **unverified**, not lossless, because the
transport exposes no equivalent completed-frame/deadtime counters.

## Conversion

Use **File → Convert Binary to HDF5...** for NDMA data. Conversion validates
the header and full-record alignment; IIO list-mode conversion also validates
complete 1,024-record frames and authenticated metadata when present.

Converted Scope HDF5 contains:

- `/waveforms` (`int16`, one row per frame);
- `/timestamps` (8 ns ticks);
- `/time_ns` (waveform-relative axis);
- channel, source timestamp, frame geometry, and frame count attributes.

Converted MCA HDF5 preserves the source NDMA version and raw event dtype. A
directly recorded HDF5 file instead uses the canonical appendable schema. Use
the project readers described in [MCA List-Mode Analysis](analyze_listmode) if
code must accept both variants.

## Storage and reproducibility checklist

- Save the configuration YAML with raw captures.
- Keep JSON/run/session sidecars beside their files.
- Never overwrite an existing capture or export.
- Confirm free disk space before long Scope runs.
- Treat a live MCA histogram snapshot as non-atomic.
- Record backend, endpoint, channel, firmware/IP version, trigger mode, and
  whether continuity was verified.
- Preserve raw coordinates in exported analysis; add calibrations as metadata
  instead of rewriting source records.
